clue.text: Dame Muriel's may console

definitions.meaning: Dame Muriel Spark's first novel bears this title
people who soothe or console the grieving

explanation.definitionFit: Muriel Spark's debut novel is titled thus, and the word also names those who soothe the sorrowful.

clue.text: Was Thoreau's a take-off?

parts.note: Thoreau wrote a book about a Massachusetts headland; the clue wonders whether such a headland is a launching point

explanation.walkthrough: Thoreau's travel book is Cape Cod; a headland jutting out to sea is the sort of place one might take off from, and the clue plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a point of land projecting into the sea, as in the title of Thoreau's book.

clue.text: Space traveller's self-identification is pidgin, but suitable

parts.note: in broken English one introduces oneself with 'me'
ET is the extra-terrestrial of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: An alien introduces itself in broken English, which is said to be fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The alien would say 'Me, ET' in pidgin; the two pieces run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for fitting or proper, a synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Scott's ancient death

parts.note: ancient means old
mortality is death, or the condition of being subject to it

explanation.surface: A question about an old death in Walter Scott's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Mortality is a novel by Sir Walter Scott, one of his Tales of My Landlord.

clue.text: Prepared to play new middle of bad duet

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the middle of the scrambled letters of duet
bad suggests the word duet is spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians make ready to perform a fresh version of a poor duet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles DUET into TUED; 'middle of' places N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that has been tuned is set up and ready for performance.

clue.text: Gun man and artist of the Old West

definitions.meaning: Eliphalet ... founded the famous firearms company
Frederic ... painted cowboys and cavalry of the American frontier

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the firearms maker and to the painter and sculptor of frontier scenes.

clue.text: Had returned a pound for children's writer

indicators.note: returned tells us to read the word had backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone got back a pound for a children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns HAD into DAH, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory and other children's books.

clue.text: Obtain soul in exchange for Tolstoy's Confession and forgiveness?

indicators.note: the letters are exchanged, i.e. swapped round into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A Faustian bargain: getting a soul in return for Tolstoy's memoir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in exchange' rearranges OBTAIN SOUL. Tolstoy wrote A Confession; the definition describes what a priest grants after confession, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: In the church, confession is followed by the priest's pardon of sins.

clue.text: Slay artist out of hand — for naming Greek feminist

indicators.note: out of hand means out of control, so the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A violent call to kill a painter, apparently over the naming of a Greek heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of hand' rearranges SLAY ARTIST; 'for naming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristophanes's heroine leads the women of Greece in a sex strike to end war, an early feminist figure.

clue.text: Send up my so carefully disguised noms de plume

indicators.note: disguised says the letters are given a new appearance, rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A writer mocks their own carefully hidden pen names.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carefully disguised' rearranges SEND UP MY SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nom de plume is a pen name, a false name used by an author.

clue.text: Cleopatra's deliverers, like afterthought

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
PS (postscript) is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: The bringers of Cleopatra's death, mentioned almost as an afterthought.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra died by snakebite, the venomous snakes being brought to her in a basket of figs.

clue.text: Tip never refused by her

parts.note: Tip is the nickname of the scapegrace brother of Dickens's heroine, who always indulged him

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' looks like a gratuity, but it is Edward 'Tip' Dorrit, whose devoted sister never denied him.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's title heroine Amy, daughter of the Marshalsea debtor, constantly gives way to her wastrel brother.

clue.text: Amis work suggests author of White Fang as third man?

parts.note: Jack London wrote White Fang
third man is a fielding position in cricket, so a player there fields

explanation.surface: An Amis novel hints at an American author playing as a third participant.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, third man is a fielding position behind the batsman on the off side; a man placed there fields.
explanation.definitionFit: London Fields is a 1989 novel by Martin Amis.

clue.text: Talk of the fourth estate

parts.note: the fourth estate is the press, so this is the jargon of newspapers

explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper writing has its own clichéd style, named after the trade of reporting.

clue.text: Strong wanderers

definitions.meaning: L.A.G. Strong wrote a novel of this title, winning the James Tait Black prize
people who roam from place to place

explanation.definitionFit: The title of L.A.G. Strong's novel is also a word for itinerant people on the move.

clue.text: Personal address of Thackeray in Christmas Books

definitions.text: Personal address of Thackeray in Christmas Books

parts.words: Personal address of Thackeray in Christmas Books
parts.note: one of Thackeray's Christmas Books is named after the place where 'we' live

explanation.walkthrough: 'Personal address' suggests a speech, but it is the road one lives on, belonging to us: the title of a Thackeray Christmas book.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's Christmas book of 1848 depicts the residents of a London road.

clue.text: Repeats no sort of lingua franca

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, putting the letters in a fresh order

parts.note: the fodder, nine letters

explanation.surface: A common tongue described as one that never repeats itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's constructed tongue was meant as an international language shared by all.

clue.text: Pocket one for Pip

parts.note: Matthew Pocket in Great Expectations teaches young Pip to be a gentleman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' looks like a verb (keep one for yourself), but it is Mr Pocket, Pip's instructor in Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Pocket is engaged to educate Pip privately, as his teacher.

clue.text: Composer in tangle

explanation.definitionFit: The French composer's surname is also a verb meaning to entangle.

clue.text: Writer reorchestrating octets for spring, festival

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

indicators.note: reorchestrating suggests the octets are rearranged into a new score

explanation.surface: A composer rescores some octets for a spring celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitsun, the Christian feast seven weeks after Easter, falls in spring.

clue.text: Delightful device diligently deployed, particularly in primitive poetry

definitions.text: Delightful device diligently deployed, particularly in primitive poetry

parts.words: Delightful device diligently deployed, particularly in primitive poetry
parts.note: the clue itself repeats initial sounds, d-d-d-d then p-p-p, describing the device it shows

explanation.walkthrough: The clue demonstrates its answer: words beginning with the same letter, a staple of Old English verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating initial consonants was the structural basis of early Germanic verse such as Beowulf.

clue.text: Some victim on the list for misanthropic Athenian

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A victim on a list, apparently some hater of mankind's.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'the list for' into the definition; it is a link, and the definition is just 'misanthropic Athenian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens turns against mankind after his friends desert him.

clue.text: Attempt to start some truly awful book

indicators.note: to start means take the starting letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone tries to begin a truly dreadful book.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a stab at something is to make an attempt.

clue.text: Advantage sea has, Rachel Carson thought?

definitions.meaning: Rachel Carson wrote a book on the shoreline titled after what the sea has

explanation.definitionFit: Having an edge is having an advantage; Carson's 1955 book is The Edge of the Sea.

clue.text: It must have been west of Steinbeck's location

definitions.text: It must have been west of Steinbeck's location

parts.words: It must have been west of Steinbeck's location
parts.note: Steinbeck's novel is set east of a garden, so the garden lies west of it

explanation.walkthrough: Steinbeck's novel is East of Eden; if the book's location lies east of the garden, the garden must lie to its west.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden is named in Steinbeck's title as the place his setting lies east of.

clue.text: Mature 24 might be listed

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the answer to 24 across, the biblical garden

explanation.surface: Fully grown entries might go onto a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges MATURE with EDEN, the answer to 24 across.
explanation.definitionFit: To enumerate is to count off or list one by one.

clue.text: Snotty Equality Jack

parts.note: 'snotty' is naval slang for a midshipman, and 'Equality Jack' is the nickname of Marryat's young hero

explanation.walkthrough: Marryat's Mr Midshipman Easy has hero Jack, a midshipman (a 'snotty') nicknamed 'Equality Jack' for his egalitarian views.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Marryat's hero Jack is the midshipman of the title Mr Midshipman Easy.

clue.text: Meeting place of chivalry had no head, even when king graced it

definitions.text: Meeting place of chivalry had no head, even when king graced it

parts.words: Meeting place of chivalry had no head, even when king graced it
parts.note: Arthur's knights met at a circular board so that no seat was the head of it, even with the king present

explanation.walkthrough: 'had no head' sounds like a missing leader, but the circular shape meant there was no head of the table.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's knights sat at a circular board so none had precedence.
